one_line: A Yadava-era scholarly leader preserving Bhaskara II’s mathematics in the Devagiri hinterland.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s, lean and wiry, with the posture of a disciplined scholar who also travels and teaches.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, medium-brown Deccan complexion, sharp dark eyes with thin arched brows, a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache; a small vertical sandalwood tilak on the forehead; default expression calm, focused and slightly intense, as if always mid-explanation.
appearance.hair: Black hair tied back into a tight topknot (kudumi-style knot) high on the back of the head, sides smooth and tidy; a narrow white cotton headband (like a simple patka strip) wraps around the forehead just above the tilak, knotted at the back with short trailing ends.
appearance.costume: He wears a light cream cotton angavastra draped over both shoulders and across the chest like a scholar’s shawl, with a subtle narrow red woven border; beneath it, a long-sleeved, collarless pale yellow kurta-style upper garment, thigh-length, made of fine cotton with simple side slits; his lower garment is a ankle-length white cotton dhoti with a reddish-brown border, wrapped in the Deccan style with neat pleats in front and a tucked-in end at the waist; he has a simple brown cloth kamarband (waist sash) securing the dhoti and holding his palm-leaf bundle; around his neck hang two modest items—a black-thread amulet and a small tulasi-bead mala; he wears plain leather sandals with toe loops, and a narrow copper bangle on his right wrist; textiles are unpatterned aside from the borders, looking practical and scholarly, not royal.
appearance.signature: A bound bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts of Bhaskara II’s works, tied with a dark red cord and held in his left hand, with a narrow stylus tucked under the cord.

ref_desc: Changadeva of Vijjalavida is a late-30s Deccan scholar with a medium-brown complexion, black hair in a topknot with a white headband, pale yellow kurta, cream angavastra, white dhoti with reddish-brown border, leather sandals, and a bound palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with dark red cord and stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Changadeva of Vijjalavida, a late-30s scholarly man from Yadava-era Deccan, shown front and three-quarter view: he has an oval face, medium-brown complexion, sharp dark eyes, thin arched brows, a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, and a small vertical sandalwood tilak; his black hair is pulled into a tight topknot high on the back of his head, with a narrow white cotton headband wrapping around his forehead and knotted at the back. He wears a pale yellow, collarless, long-sleeved kurta-style upper garment to mid-thigh, made of plain cotton, over which a light cream angavastra with a narrow red border is draped over both shoulders and across his chest; his lower garment is a white cotton dhoti with a reddish-brown border, wrapped neatly to his ankles in Deccan style, held by a brown cloth kamarband at the waist. Show a black-thread amulet and a simple tulasi-bead mala at his neck, a narrow copper bangle on his right wrist, and modest brown leather sandals; no royal jewellery. In his left hand he carries his signature prop: a bound bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tied with a dark red cord, with a thin stylus tucked under the cord. Use a restrained palette of cream, white, pale yellow, reddish-brown, dark red, brown leather, and his natural medium-brown skin, and keep the design dignified, modest, and historically grounded while maintaining clear, consistent anime-style features for easy redrawing.
